title: Hierarchical Inheritance
summary: Master Hierarchical Inheritance in Java: one superclass shared by multiple sibling subclasses, understanding sibling isolation, and structuring domain hierarchies.
learningObjectives: Define Hierarchical Inheritance: one superclass extended by multiple subclasses
Understand the principle of sibling isolation (siblings cannot access each other's unique code)
Centralize common business logic in the shared superclass
Specialize each child branch with domain-specific behaviors
Design practical hierarchical systems (Shapes, Notifications, Banking Accounts)
expectedOutcomes: Ability to architect clean 1-to-many class hierarchies in Java
Clear recognition that sibling subclasses operate with complete isolation from one another

activities.title: The Sibling Talents Analogy
activities.content:
Imagine a parent who has two children: a son who is a professional violinist and a daughter who is an airline pilot.

Both children inherited the same last name, address, and biological traits from their parent.

However:
- Can the violinist fly a commercial passenger jet just because his sister is a pilot? **No!**
- Can the pilot play a violin concerto just because her brother is a violinist? **No!**

In Java, **Hierarchical Inheritance** works the exact same way:
- Multiple child classes extend the same parent class.
- All children share the parent's fields and methods.
- But each child is **completely isolated** from its siblings! Neither child can access or execute the specialized methods of its sibling.

activities.title: Hierarchical Inheritance and Sibling Isolation
Hierarchical Architecture: The Notification System
activities.description: See how EmailNotification and SMSNotification specialize a single Notification superclass.

steps.description: Notification is the single shared superclass with recipient, message, and logDispatch().
EmailNotification extends Notification and adds subject and sendEmail().
SMSNotification extends Notification and adds characterLimit and sendSMS().
Both siblings reuse logDispatch() cleanly, but maintain complete isolation from each other.

activities.title: Hierarchical Inheritance: Geometric Shapes
activities.description: Observe how Circle and Rectangle both extend Shape while maintaining unique calculations.

steps.description: Shape is the common superclass holding name and printName().
Circle and Rectangle both extend Shape (Hierarchical Inheritance).
Circle adds radius, while Rectangle adds width and height.
Each calculates its area independently using its own private attributes.

questions.question: What is Hierarchical Inheritance in Java?
options: One child class inheriting from multiple parent classes
Multiple subclasses extending the same single superclass
A class having multiple main methods
A package containing multiple classes
questions.explanation: Hierarchical inheritance is a 1-to-many relationship where multiple subclasses extend a single shared parent class.

questions.question: What are subclasses that extend the same superclass called?
options: Twin classes
Sibling classes
Cousin classes
Nested classes
questions.explanation: Subclasses that share the same direct superclass are known as sibling classes.

questions.question: Can sibling class A directly access a method defined exclusively in sibling class B?
options: Yes, sibling classes share all methods
No, sibling classes have strict isolation and cannot see each other's specialized methods
Only if both classes have the same constructor arguments
Only if the superclass is abstract
questions.explanation: Under sibling isolation, sibling classes know nothing about each other's unique methods.

questions.question: Where should logic shared by all siblings be placed?
options: Duplicated into every sibling class separately
Centralized in the common superclass
In a separate interface file
Inside the main method
questions.explanation: Shared logic belongs in the common superclass so that all sibling subclasses can inherit it.

questions.question: If Dog and Cat both extend Animal, what happens in heap memory when instantiating one Dog and one Cat?
options: Only one object is created, shared between Dog and Cat
Two distinct objects are created on the heap, each with its own state
Java throws an OutOfMemoryError due to sibling conflict
Dog and Cat share the exact same reference pointer
questions.explanation: Two distinct objects are created in heap memory, each allocated independently.

questions.question: Can sibling subclasses have different fields from each other?
options: No, all siblings must have the exact same fields
Yes, each sibling can define unique fields that fit its specialized purpose
Only if the fields are static
Only if the fields are integers
questions.explanation: Each sibling subclass can add whatever unique fields and methods it requires.

questions.question: If class Dog extends Animal and class Cat extends Animal, what happens if Animal's eat() method is updated?
options: Only Dog gets the update
Both Dog and Cat automatically inherit the updated behavior
Neither gets the update until both are renamed
The program fails compilation
questions.explanation: Because both extend Animal, any modification to the parent's logic immediately updates all sibling subclasses.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Circle and Rectangle if both extend Shape?
options: Parent and child
Sibling subclasses with isolation
Grandparent and grandchild
Interface and implementation
questions.explanation: Circle and Rectangle are sibling subclasses that extend Shape.

questions.question: Does hierarchical inheritance violate Java's single inheritance rule?
options: Yes, because the parent has multiple children
No, because each individual child class extends only ONE direct superclass
Yes, unless interfaces are used
Only in private packages
questions.explanation: Each subclass extends only one direct superclass, fully obeying Java's single inheritance rule.

questions.question: Can a superclass call methods defined in its sibling child classes?
options: Yes, the parent can call any child method
No, inheritance flows strictly downward from parent to child
Yes, if the parent uses super.childMethod()
Only if the child class is final
questions.explanation: Inheritance flows downward. A superclass cannot access unique methods declared in its subclasses.

interviewQA.question: What is Hierarchical Inheritance and when should it be used?
interviewQA.answer: Hierarchical inheritance is an OOP structure where multiple subclasses extend a single common superclass. It should be used when multiple distinct entities share common attributes and behaviors that can be abstracted into a generalized parent type (e.g., Circle, Rectangle, Triangle all extending Shape).

interviewQA.question: What is sibling isolation in hierarchical inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Sibling isolation refers to the fact that sibling subclasses (classes that share the same superclass) have zero direct access to each other's specialized members. Each subclass extends the parent independently and cannot invoke methods or read fields that exist only in a sibling subclass.

interviewQA.question: How does hierarchical inheritance simplify code maintenance?
interviewQA.answer: Hierarchical inheritance centralizes shared state and operations in one superclass. A bug fix, security patch, or performance optimization applied to the superclass automatically propagates to all sibling subclasses, eliminating redundant edits and code divergence.

interviewQA.question: How does polymorphism interact with hierarchical inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Hierarchical inheritance forms the foundation of subtype polymorphism. A superclass reference (e.g., Shape s) can hold an instance of any sibling subclass (new Circle() or new Rectangle()). This enables collections of heterogeneous sibling objects (List<Shape>) to be processed uniformly.

interviewQA.question: Can sibling classes have different constructors?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. Each sibling subclass defines its own constructors with whatever parameters are required to initialize its unique fields, while chaining to the superclass constructor via super() to initialize common parent fields.

interviewQA.question: What happens if two sibling classes declare fields with identical names?
interviewQA.answer: There is no conflict whatsoever. Because sibling classes have isolated scopes, a field declared in SiblingA (e.g., 'int id') is completely distinct from a field declared in SiblingB ('int id'). They occupy separate memory locations in their respective object instances.

activities.title: 10-Point Mastery Checklist: Hierarchical Inheritance
checklist: I can define Hierarchical Inheritance clearly
I understand the 1-to-many relationship (one parent, multiple children)
I understand the principle of sibling isolation
I know that sibling classes cannot access each other's unique methods
I know that each child extends only one direct superclass
I know how to centralize common logic in the shared parent class
I can design a hierarchy with 3 or more sibling subclasses
I know that updating the parent updates all sibling classes automatically
I understand how sibling objects exist independently in heap memory
I can build a working hierarchical inheritance system in Java

practiceProblems.title: Hierarchical Bank Accounts
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a hierarchical bank account system:
1. Shared superclass `Account` with field `String accNumber`, `double balance`, and method `void showBalance()` printing `accNumber + " balance: $" + balance`
2. Sibling 1 `SavingsAccount` extending `Account` with method `void applyBonus()` that adds `10.0` to `balance` and prints `"Bonus added! New balance: $" + balance`
3. Sibling 2 `CheckingAccount` extending `Account` with method `void deductMaintenanceFee()` that subtracts `5.0` from `balance` and prints `"Fee deducted! New balance: $" + balance`
In `Main.main()`, instantiate a `SavingsAccount` (`accNumber = "SAV-101", balance = 500.0`) and call `showBalance()` then `applyBonus()`. Instantiate a `CheckingAccount` (`accNumber = "CHK-202", balance = 200.0`) and call `showBalance()` then `deductMaintenanceFee()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
SAV-101 balance: $500.0
Bonus added! New balance: $510.0
CHK-202 balance: $200.0
Fee deducted! New balance: $195.0
hints: Both SavingsAccount and CheckingAccount extend Account.
Each sibling accesses the inherited balance field.

practiceProblems.title: Hierarchical UI Components From Scratch
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Write a complete program from scratch demonstrating hierarchical inheritance:
1. Superclass `UIWidget` with field `String widgetId` and method `void render()` printing `"Rendering widget: " + widgetId`.
2. Sibling 1 `Button` extending `UIWidget` with field `String label` and method `void click()` printing `"Button '" + label + "' clicked!"`.
3. Sibling 2 `TextBox` extending `UIWidget` with field `String text` and method `void typeText(String input)` updating `text` to `input` and printing `"TextBox text updated to: '" + text + "'"`.
4. In `Main.main()`, test `Button` (`widgetId = "btn-submit", label = "Submit"`) and `TextBox` (`widgetId = "tb-username", text = ""`). Render both widgets and call their respective unique methods.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Rendering widget: btn-submit
Button 'Submit' clicked!
Rendering widget: tb-username
TextBox text updated to: 'john_doe'
hints: Both Button and TextBox extend UIWidget.
Demonstrate sibling isolation by ensuring Button has no typeText() and TextBox has no click().

practiceProblems.title: Tri-Sibling Media Player Hierarchy
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Create a shared superclass `MediaFile` with `String fileName` and `int durationSec`, and method `void printMeta()` printing `fileName + " (" + durationSec + "s)"`.
Create three sibling subclasses extending `MediaFile`:
- `AudioFile` with `int bitRateKbps` and method `void playAudio()` printing `"Playing audio at " + bitRateKbps + " kbps"`
- `VideoFile` with `String resolution` and method `void playVideo()` printing `"Streaming video in " + resolution`
- `ImageFile` with `String dimensions` and method `void displayImage()` printing `"Showing image at " + dimensions`
In `Main.main()`, instantiate one of each, set their fields, print their metadata, and invoke their unique playback/display method.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
song.mp3 (210s)
Playing audio at 320 kbps
movie.mp4 (7200s)
Streaming video in 1080p
photo.jpg (0s)
Showing image at 1920x1080
hints: AudioFile, VideoFile, and ImageFile all extend MediaFile.
Each class maintains its own unique fields and methods.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Sibling Isolation Violation
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The following program fails compilation because someone tried to invoke `fly()` (defined in `Bird`) on a `Dog` object, violating sibling isolation. Fix the main method so each sibling only calls valid methods, producing the expected output.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Max is sleeping.
Max says Woof!
Robin is sleeping.
Robin is flying in the sky!
hints: Dog cannot call fly() because fly() belongs exclusively to Bird.
Instantiate a Bird object to call fly().

practiceProblems.title: Hierarchical Cloud Resource Provisioning
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a cloud resource manager:
1. Superclass `CloudResource` with `protected String resourceId`, `protected String region`, and constructor `public CloudResource(String id, String region)`.
   - Method `public void logProvision()` printing `"Provisioned " + resourceId + " in " + region`
2. Sibling 1 `ComputeInstance` extending `CloudResource`:
   - `private int vCpuCount`
   - Constructor `public ComputeInstance(String id, String region, int vCpu)` calling `super(id, region)`
   - Method `public void launch()` calling `logProvision()` and printing `"Compute instance running with " + vCpuCount + " vCPUs."`
3. Sibling 2 `StorageBucket` extending `CloudResource`:
   - `private int capacityGB`
   - Constructor `public StorageBucket(String id, String region, int capacity)` calling `super(id, region)`
   - Method `public void mount()` calling `logProvision()` and printing `"Storage bucket mounted with " + capacityGB + " GB storage."`
In `Main.main()`, test both siblings: `ComputeInstance("vm-prod-01", "us-east-1", 8)` and `StorageBucket("s3-logs-bucket", "us-west-2", 500)`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Provisioned vm-prod-01 in us-east-1
Compute instance running with 8 vCPUs.
Provisioned s3-logs-bucket in us-west-2
Storage bucket mounted with 500 GB storage.
hints: Both ComputeInstance and StorageBucket inherit from CloudResource.
Both invoke logProvision() through inherited access.
